items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective Evaluation), the report thoroughly validates the VOS framework on the 1000x2000 Lasso dataset, showing that VOS-AG-II with function restart achieves dramatically lower objective values than the Proximal Gradient baseline at fixed budgets (e.g., 36.5645 vs. 55.0602 at k=50, reaching the certified optimum 36.564360 by k~95) and reaches the 1e-7 tolerance roughly 4x faster across relative gap (52 vs. 215 iterations), absolute gap (65 vs. 257), and fixed-point residual (83 vs. 318). Furthermore, it rigorously quantifies the steeper late-stage linear convergence rate of VOS-AG-II+restart (0.569/iter after support identification at k=52, closely matching the restricted-curvature prediction 0.527) versus PG's prolonged sub-linear plateau (O(k^-0.55) until k=231) and slower local rate (0.854/iter). Both methodology and quantitative execution substantially exceed a standard benchmark paper through KKT-polished duality certification (2e-12 floor), cancellation-free gap computation, restart-driven 2x+ speedups over plain VOS-AG-II, diagnosis of VOS-AG-I's non-sparse stagnation, and multi-lambda/initialization robustness sweeps.

items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode B (mechanistic and robustness validation), the report thoroughly fulfills all three technical aspects: handling non-smooth L1 regularization via the proximal operator, achieving fast convergence without divergence or stagnation to a KKT-certified optimum (66 vs. 258 iterations for PG), and implementing adaptive function restart to eliminate momentum-induced overshooting. Beyond the original paper's analysis, the report provides significantly deeper mechanistic insights by disentangling global variable-splitting damping from adaptive restart under local restricted strong convexity (mu_S = 7.515 vs. global mu = 0), explaining why VOS-AG-I stalls due to non-sparse convex combinations while VOS-AG-II identifies the support early, and validating robustness across multiple lambda values, random initializations that excite the 1000-dimensional null space, and condition numbers up to 10^5.
